name: Kuwait
summary: Kuwait imposes no personal income tax: no tax on individuals' capital gains or dividends, and no wealth, inheritance or gift tax. Corporate tax (15%) applies only to foreign-owned businesses; Kuwaiti and GCC-owned companies pay zakat and other levies instead, and large multinationals the 15% DMTT. Residence for foreigners is largely tied to employment or sponsorship.

regimes.name: Kuwait residence
regimes.eligibility: Any legal resident; Kuwait law does not define individual tax residence.

capital_gains.summary: No personal income tax, so no tax on individuals' capital gains (PwC).

open_questions: Succession rules for non-Muslim foreigners not verified.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Succession, not tax, is the issue: personal status law based on Sharia governs the estates of Muslims (fixed shares; a son typically takes twice a daughter's share; at most one third freely disposable by will to non-heirs). How estates of non-Muslim foreigners are handled (law of nationality, own religious rules, or Sharia by default) was not verified here; non-Muslim families should take local legal advice.

residency.tax_residency_test: Kuwait tax law does not define individual tax residence (PwC); there is no personal income tax.

routes.name: Residence permit (sponsorship / investor)
routes.requirements: Residence for foreigners is generally tied to an employer or family sponsor. A newer foreigners' residence law (2024) provides for investor and long-term residence; terms not verified.

corporate.summary: 15% CIT only on foreign 'corporate bodies' and the foreign-owned share of GCC companies doing business in Kuwait. Kuwaiti shareholding companies pay 1% zakat and 1% KFAS; a 15% DMTT applies to MNE groups with revenue of EUR 750M+ from 2025.

sources.title: Kuwait - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income (last reviewed 22 Jul 2026)

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed; no US-Kuwait income tax treaty, and no Kuwaiti tax to credit.
